observations: TypeScript became GitHub's most-used language in August 2025, ahead of Python and JavaScript.
Java and C# were fourth and fifth; PHP, Shell, C++, HCL, and Go were also in GitHub's 2025 top ten.
The combined JavaScript and TypeScript ecosystem remained larger than Python on GitHub.
Python adoption increased by seven percentage points from 2024 to 2025 and spans AI, data science, and backend work.
Rust was the most admired programming language in the 2025 survey at 72 percent.
Python developers showed strong interest in Rust and Go for performance-oriented systems work.
The report is based on 24,534 developers across 194 countries.
TypeScript had the strongest five-year real-world usage rise; Rust, Go, and Kotlin also gained share.
Top stated next-language adoption included Go 11 percent, Rust 10 percent, Python 7 percent, Kotlin 6 percent, and TypeScript 6 percent.

repository_evidence.fact: FR-023 requires an evidence-derived language/tooling mix and rejects marketing breadth as a capacity objective.
B007/B015 planning explicitly covers Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Rust, Go, Java, C/C++, SQL, shell, JSON/YAML/TOML, diffs, stack traces, paths, and tool JSON.
B014 delegates language percentages/tiers to B015 and requires the canonical language target policy before training admission.

triggers: material shift in public repository language distribution
MSTR evaluation shows repeated product-critical weakness
source availability or rights make a replay floor infeasible

replay_policy.flexible_allocation_rule: After all minima are satisfied, remaining language/tooling capacity is assigned by stage-specific product/evaluation evidence. Long-tail total may not exceed its cap without a canonical B015 amendment.
replay_policy.no_silent_zero_rule: A core or secondary target with admissible source material may not be silently omitted; any inability to meet its minimum requires a canonical exception with exact reason and impact analysis.

scope.interpretation: Replay floors are capacity-preservation guardrails, not market-share estimates or claims of optimal final mixture weights.

stage_manifest_rules: Declare the accounting unit and denominator used for language/tooling weights.
Declare core, secondary, tooling/config, and long-tail totals; all allocated shares must sum to 100 percent of the language/tooling slice.
Meet every aggregate, per-language, and tooling-group replay floor unless a canonical B015 amendment explicitly changes the policy.
Do not infer software-role CODE/FIM/TEST/DIFF ratios from B015; those remain stage-specific under the Data Constitution.
Preserve provenance, rights, contamination, dedup, benchmark exclusion, and verifier-health gates from MSTR-DATA-CONSTITUTION-v0.
Do not admit private user repositories or production traces by default.

long_tail.admission_rule: A long-tail language receives stage allocation only when product tasks, evaluation failures, customer/developer demand, repository distribution, or strategic platform evidence justifies the capacity. Marketing completeness is not evidence.
